Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Because no prior claims exist, the first registration wave focuses on biologically motivated, falsifiable selective-dependency hypotheses using measured binary genomic or assay predictors. Dependency scores are interpreted such that stronger dependency is more negative; therefore, for expected stronger dependency in exposed cells versus comparator cells, the raw exposed-minus-comparator mean difference should be negative, and we set the claim direction to -1 so that a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency. For MDM2 and USP7, the prediction is that loss of TP53 reduces pathway dependence, producing weaker dependency and therefore a less negative, i.e. raw positive, exposed-minus-comparator difference; these claims use direction +1. The main oncogene hypotheses are: BRAF V600E versus wild-type cells should show stronger BRAF dependency; KRAS-mutant versus wild-type cells should show stronger KRAS dependency; EGFR-amplified versus non-amplified cells should show stronger EGFR dependency; and ERBB2-amplified versus non-amplified cells should show stronger ERBB2 dependency. The chromatin/replication hypotheses are: SMARCA4-loss cells should depend more strongly on the paralog SMARCA2; MSI-high cells should depend more strongly on WRN; and KEAP1-loss cells should depend more strongly on NFE2L2/NRF2 due to activated oxidative-stress pathways. The MYC-amplification models test whether MYC-driven transcriptional or translational stress selectively increases dependency on DHX9 and RPL11. The KRAS interaction tests whether KRAS dependency is more pronounced in lung adenocarcinoma than in the complement subtype while holding the same KRAS-mutation contrast. These comparisons are registered as unresolved because evidence in this supplied dataset has not yet been estimated. For practical significance, I will use the stated 10% relative-change threshold relative to the comparator mean where feasible, while also judging absolute magnitude against the observed score distribution, since dependency scores are arbitrary continuous values with typical SDs around 0.18-0.4. I will not infer causality or generalizability from this panel before independent validation and specificity checks.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: I assessed all twelve discovery estimates on their signed scale, without re-multiplying by direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is negative, i.e. stronger dependency in exposed cells; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means less negative/weak dependency in exposed cells. The strongest supported dataset findings are H5 SMARCA4 loss -> SMARCA2 dependency and H6 MSI-high -> WRN dependency: both have very large positive signed effects, precise intervals far from zero, and estimated raw differences hundreds of percent relative to approximate comparator means. Both also remain meaningful after multiplicity for 12 initial tests. H10 is accepted as a dataset-level association in the predicted direction: TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency, with a large positive signed effect and interval excluding zero. H8 is rejected as originally hypothesized, but the evidence is extremely strong in the opposite direction: signed estimate is about -0.796 for the expected stronger-dependency direction, implying raw KEAP1-loss cells have much less negative NFE2L2 dependency. I therefore reject the original H8 claim but register a reversed H8-linked proposal. H3 EGFR amplification is only borderline: the point estimate is near the 10% relative threshold and nominal significance is at the margin, but the interval includes zero and the result would not survive family-wise correction. I keep it unresolved/active rather than accept. H2 and H7 are unresolved/deferred because their point effects are small and not statistically supported, although confidence intervals can reach the 10% practical threshold and are not definitive equivalence tests. H1, H4, H9, H11, and H12 are rejected/closed because effects are tiny or point away from the hypothesis and do not support clinically meaningful differences. Potential confounding remains because all analyses are observational within one lung panel and could be affected by library/technical variation or genomic co-occurrence; no causal claim is made. I request validation for H10 because it is an accepted, large, less-canonical dependency-TP53-loss association and independent evidence would clarify whether this is robust before further interpretive weight is placed on it. Future proposals follow up accepted findings within a major library, test related SWI/SNF/repair predictors, assess subtype consistency, and explore one constructed-marker subgroup for the WRN effect.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

record.narrative: The independent validation for H10 is decisive. R13, signed to the +1 hypothesis direction, estimates a raw association of about +0.448 for TP53 loss versus wild type on dependency_USP7, with an independently adjusted interval [0.347, 0.549] excluding zero. This is far beyond the 10% practical-significance scale and is concordant with the discovery estimate R10 (+0.396, 95% CI [0.325, 0.467]). I therefore keep H10 accepted: in this lung panel, TP53-loss cells show substantially weaker USP7 dependency, i.e. a less negative CRISPR score, than TP53-wild-type cells. This remains an observational dataset association, not evidence of causality or external generalizability. I also reassess the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 claim H13. R8 gives a signed +0.796 estimate for the positive direction [0.776, 0.816], meaning KEAP1-loss cells have markedly less negative NFE2L2 dependency scores, not stronger dependency as originally hypothesized in H8. The effect is huge relative to the observed NFE2L2 dependency scale and the interval is narrow. Because the direction was discovered after testing the opposite hypothesis, I accept it as a dataset-level association with more caution than pre-specified findings, but the evidence is strong enough to support the conclusion that KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency in these data. The most useful next analyses are robustness and subgroup-consistency checks for the accepted associations. I register a KEAP1-loss reversed-effect check restricted to the Avana library (parent H13), a SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2-dependency check outside the Avana library (parent H5), and a WRN MSI-high effect restricted to the adenocarcinoma subtype (parent H6). These complement the existing Avana-library checks and lineage interactions. If the accepted effects persist under library restriction and within the dominant subtype, they become more robust dataset associations; if not, technical or biological heterogeneity should limit interpretation. Further broad exploration can later test additional pathway hypotheses, such as MYC amplification with core transcriptional or mitotic dependencies, but the immediate priority is to strengthen or localize the currently accepted findings.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: The current accepted dataset associations are strong but observational. To protect against overinterpreting them as biologically specific rather than broad fitness/screen artifacts, I register four negative-control comparisons using dependency_POLR2A for the same predictors behind accepted claims: SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, TP53 loss, and KEAP1 loss. These are pre-registered as expected null/unresolved; we will judge whether any control association reaches a meaningful magnitude relative to the comparator mean and interval width, not simply whether p is nominal. For robustness of accepted effects, I add context heterogeneity checks: whether the SMARCA4 loss effect on SMARCA2 differs by ARID1A loss, whether WRN/MSI and USP7/TP53 effects differ by mutation burden, and whether the reversed KEAP1 loss effect on NFE2L2 persists within the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype. I also add two new pathway hypotheses to broaden exploration: EGFR-amplified cells may be more dependent on secretory/receptor-trafficking machinery, proxied by TMED10; and PIK3CA-mutant cells may show weaker upstream EGFR dependency if PI3K activation bypasses EGFR signaling. Direction convention: for dependency scores, more negative means stronger dependency. Thus, for hypotheses of stronger dependency in exposed cells, direction is -1; for hypotheses of weaker dependency in exposed cells, direction is +1. Controls use anticipated_direction 0 with arbitrary direction +1 to allow interpretation of signed estimates. All proposals are unresolved because no evidence exists for these specific comparisons yet, and none is treated as causal or generalizable.

H10 is accepted as a dataset-level association in the predicted direction: TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency, with a large positive signed effect and interval excluding zero. H1, H4, H9, H11, and H12 are rejected/closed because effects are tiny or point away from the hypothesis and do not support clinically meaningful differences. The first goal is robustness: restrict each accepted predictor-dependency pair to the majority Avana library (H14, H15, H16, H23), and test whether the two largest dependencies remain in the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype (H25, H29). record.narrative:
I assessed every new discovery estimate on the signed scale already supplied, without reapplying direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is more negative, i.e. stronger CRISPR dependency in exposed cells. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means less negative/weaker dependency in exposed cells.

The robustness checks for the three largest accepted associations are essentially confirmatory. H14 (R14) gives SMARCA4 loss vs SMARCA4 wild type within the Avana library a signed effect of +0.781 [0.760, 0.802], very close to the full-population H5 estimate and far from zero; cell counts are adequate. I accept it as a robust Avana-specific dataset association. H15 (R15) for MSI-high vs non-MSI WRN dependency in Avana is +0.794 [0.764, 0.825], again extremely large and precise; I accept it. H16 (R16) for TP53 loss USP7 dependency in Avana is +0.405 [0.330, 0.479], concordant with discovery R10 and validated R13; I accept it as robust in the major library. H23 (R17), the reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association in Avana, is +0.796 [0.774, 0.818], nearly identical to the full-population reversed estimate; I accept it as strong evidence that the reversed direction is not driven by library composition. H25 (R18) shows MSI-high WRN dependency within adenocarcinoma at +0.784 [0.748, 0.820], and H29 (R21) shows KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 within adenocarcinoma at +0.793 [0.769, 0.817]. These are subgroup-specific consistency checks, not effect-modification tests, and both support persistence in the dominant lineage subtype.

H28 (R20), the USP7/TP53 interaction by mutation burden >=5, is inconclusive: signed estimate +0.133 [-0.010, 0.275]. The interval crosses zero and, relative to the USP7 dependency scale, spans roughly small negative to very large positive relative change. It does not support a meaningful effect modification, but it does not rule one out. I keep it unresolved and defer it rather than chase a null/ambiguous interaction. H27 (R19) is invalid because the subgroup interaction design has an empty comparison cell (no TP53-loss MSI-high? Actually no exposed complement for the chosen mutation-burden cut; MSI-high appears fully contained in the high-burden stratum). It is not evaluable as specified; I close this investigation and register an alternative high-burden mean-difference check instead.

The POLR2A negative controls provide partial specificity evidence but are not uniformly definitive. H30 (R22) is a clean negative: SMARCA4 loss has signed +0.005 [-0.014, 0.024] on POLR2A. Even the upper bound is about 9% of the POLR2A mean scale, below the 10% practical threshold, so I reject the pre-specified meaningful positive control association and close it. H31 (R23) for MSI-high POLR2A is small in point estimate but imprecise: +0.0035 [-0.028, 0.035]; the interval includes zero and can reach beyond 10% relative magnitude, so I keep it unresolved/deferred. H32 (R24) for TP53 loss POLR2A is signed negative: -0.014 [-0.034, 0.006]. It rejects the original positive direction because the upper positive bound is far below practical significance, but the lower bound suggests a possible opposite small-to-moderate association. Rather than force the original arbitrary control direction to accommodate this, I reject H32 for its original direction and register a reversed POLR2A/TP53 proposal. H33 (R25) for KEAP1 loss POLR2A is +0.007 [-0.013, 0.027], small but with an upper bound just over the 10% relative scale; unresolved/deferred. Overall, the accepted dependency-specific effects are one to two orders of magnitude larger than these control estimates, so the controls make pure global technical confounding less likely, but two controls remain too imprecise to claim exact nulls.

Multiplicity matters. The new wave contains many related checks, but the accepted large effects have intervals so far from zero that family-wise or Bonferroni-style caution would not overturn them. Borderline control/interaction claims are not upgraded to accept because their intervals remain compatible with null or small effects. The main residual concerns are observational confounding by genomic co-occurrence, technical variation despite library restriction, and the post hoc nature of the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 claim. No causal or external-generizability conclusion is drawn. I request validation for H13 because it is the strongest accepted finding whose direction was discovered after the original hypothesis failed; independent evidence would materially reduce the risk that it is a fluke or artifact of the particular split or model.

Iteration 2/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

These are pre-registered as expected null/unresolved; we will judge whether any control association reaches a meaningful magnitude relative to the comparator mean and interval width, not simply whether p is nominal. For robustness of accepted effects, I add context heterogeneity checks: whether the SMARCA4 loss effect on SMARCA2 differs by ARID1A loss, whether WRN/MSI and USP7/TP53 effects differ by mutation burden, and whether the reversed KEAP1 loss effect on NFE2L2 persists within the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype. Direction convention: for dependency scores, more negative means stronger dependency. Thus, for hypotheses of stronger dependency in exposed cells, direction is -1; for hypotheses of weaker dependency in exposed cells, direction is +1. Controls use anticipated_direction 0 with arbitrary direction +1 to allow interpretation of signed estimates. record.narrative: The independent validation delivered for H13 resolves the post hoc reversal of the KEAP1-loss hypothesis. Signed to the +1 direction, discovery evidence R8 estimated a raw association of +0.796 for KEAP1-loss versus KEAP1-wild-type cells on dependency_NFE2L2, 95% CI [0.776, 0.816]. Independent validation R26 estimated +0.799 with an independently adjusted interval [0.769, 0.829], excluding zero and with adequate cell counts. In raw dependency-score terms, this means KEAP1-loss cells have NFE2L2 dependency scores about 0.8 units less negative than KEAP1 wild-type cells, i.e. markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The magnitude is far larger than the 10% practical-significance threshold used for this task. I therefore keep H13 accepted and close further investigation of the original reversed claim. The same validation also reinforces rejection of H8, which pre-specified the opposite direction (stronger NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells): both discovery and validation are opposite to the original hypothesized direction. This remains an observational association in the supplied lung-panel dataset, not evidence of causality or external generalizability. Broadly, the dataset now supports four large, internally robust dependency associations: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H5/R5; Avana-restricted H14/R14); MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency (H6/R6; Avana-restricted H15/R15; adenocarcinoma subgroup H25/R18); TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency (H10/R10, validated R13; Avana-restricted H16/R16); and KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13/R8 and validated R26; Avana-restricted H23/R17; adenocarcinoma subgroup H29/R21). Each of these effects is precise and large relative to the outcome scale. Negative or low-utility findings include the absence of a meaningful BRAF-V600E association with dependency_BRAF (H1/R1), absence of a meaningful ERBB2-amplification association with dependency_ERBB2 (H4/R4), and absence of MYC-amplification effects on dependency_DHX9 and dependency_RPL11 (H11/R11, H12/R12). POLR2A negative controls generally make a global technical confound less likely for the large accepted effects, although not every control is perfectly precise: SMARCA4-loss POLR2A is a clean negative (H30/R22), TP53-loss POLR2A rejects the original positive direction but may leave a small opposite effect (H32/R24, refinement H38), and MSI-high and KEAP1-loss POLR2A controls remain too imprecise to claim exact nulls (H31/R23, H33/R25). Residual uncertainty concerns effect modification and robustness: non-Avana checks for USP7/TP53 and NFE2L2/KEAP1 are pending (H36, H37), subtype and mutation-burden interactions remain mostly unresolved, and several smaller pathway questions remain underpowered or imprecise, including KRAS mutation on KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification on EGFR dependency, and TP53 loss on MDM2 dependency. The most informative next analysis is to test whether the validated KEAP1-loss reversed effect on NFE2L2 differs by adenocarcinoma subtype rather than merely persisting within it, while also prioritizing pending non-Avana robustness checks, the reversed POLR2A/TP53 control, and biologically plausible follow-ups such as STK11-loss modification of KRAS dependency, WRN/MSI within high mutation burden, and broad WRN/MYC replication-stress hypotheses. The newly registered NFE2L2/KEAP1 subtype interaction complements the already accepted adenocarcinoma mean difference and will better separate persistence from effect modification.

These are pre-registered as expected null/unresolved; we will judge whether any control association reaches a meaningful magnitude relative to the comparator mean and interval width, not simply whether p is nominal. For robustness of accepted effects, I add context heterogeneity checks: whether the SMARCA4 loss effect on SMARCA2 differs by ARID1A loss, whether WRN/MSI and USP7/TP53 effects differ by mutation burden, and whether the reversed KEAP1 loss effect on NFE2L2 persists within the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype. I also add two new pathway hypotheses to broaden exploration: EGFR-amplified cells may be more dependent on secretory/receptor-trafficking machinery, proxied by TMED10; and PIK3CA-mutant cells may show weaker upstream EGFR dependency if PI3K activation bypasses EGFR signaling. Direction convention: for dependency scores, more negative means stronger dependency. Thus, for hypotheses of stronger dependency in exposed cells, direction is -1; for hypotheses of weaker dependency in exposed cells, direction is +1. Controls use anticipated_direction 0 with arbitrary direction +1 to allow interpretation of signed estimates. The second goal is specificity: use dependency_POLR2A as a broadly essential transcriptional-machinery control for the same predictors (H30, H31, H32, H33). A large POLR2A association would suggest a more general fitness/technical association, whereas small or interval-bounded estimates would make the corresponding dependency-specific interpretations more plausible. The third goal is effect heterogeneity: test whether the WRN/MSI and USP7/TP53 associations vary by mutation burden (H27, H28). I defer the non-Avana SMARCA4 check and SMARCA2 x ARID1A interaction until we know whether library and subtype patterns materially modify the accepted SMARCA2 effect. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is more negative, i.e. stronger CRISPR dependency in exposed cells. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means less negative/weaker dependency in exposed cells.\n\nThe robustness checks for the three largest accepted associations are essentially confirmatory. H14 (R14) gives SMARCA4 loss vs SMARCA4 wild type within the Avana library a signed effect of +0.781 [0.760, 0.802], very close to the full-population H5 estimate and far from zero; cell counts are adequate. I accept it as a robust Avana-specific dataset association. H15 (R15) for MSI-high vs non-MSI WRN dependency in Avana is +0.794 [0.764, 0.825], again extremely large and precise; I accept it. H16 (R16) for TP53 loss USP7 dependency in Avana is +0.405 [0.330, 0.479], concordant with discovery R10 and validated R13; I accept it as robust in the major library. H23 (R17), the reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association in Avana, is +0.796 [0.774, 0.818], nearly identical to the full-population reversed estimate; I accept it as strong evidence that the reversed direction is not driven by library composition. H25 (R18) shows MSI-high WRN dependency within adenocarcinoma at +0.784 [0.748, 0.820], and H29 (R21) shows KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 within adenocarcinoma at +0.793 [0.769, 0.817]. These are subgroup-specific consistency checks, not effect-modification tests, and both support persistence in the dominant lineage subtype.\n\nH28 (R20), the USP7/TP53 interaction by mutation burden >=5, is inconclusive: signed estimate +0.133 [-0.010, 0.275]. The interval crosses zero and, relative to the USP7 dependency scale, spans roughly small negative to very large positive relative change. It does not support a meaningful effect modification, but it does not rule one out. I keep it unresolved and defer it rather than chase a null/ambiguous interaction. H27 (R19) is invalid because the subgroup interaction design has an empty comparison cell (no TP53-loss MSI-high? Actually no exposed complement for the chosen mutation-burden cut; MSI-high appears fully contained in the high-burden stratum). It is not evaluable as specified; I close this investigation and register an alternative high-burden mean-difference check instead.\n\nThe POLR2A negative controls provide partial specificity evidence but are not uniformly definitive. H30 (R22) is a clean negative: SMARCA4 loss has signed +0.005 [-0.014, 0.024] on POLR2A. Even the upper bound is about 9% of the POLR2A mean scale, below the 10% practical threshold, so I reject the pre-specified meaningful positive control association and close it. H31 (R23) for MSI-high POLR2A is small in point estimate but imprecise: +0.0035 [-0.028, 0.035]; the interval includes zero and can reach beyond 10% relative magnitude, so I keep it unresolved/deferred. H32 (R24) for TP53 loss POLR2A is signed negative: -0.014 [-0.034, 0.006]. It rejects the original positive direction because the upper positive bound is far below practical significance, but the lower bound suggests a possible opposite small-to-moderate association. Rather than force the original arbitrary control direction to accommodate this, I reject H32 for its original direction and register a reversed POLR2A/TP53 proposal. H33 (R25) for KEAP1 loss POLR2A is +0.007 [-0.013, 0.027], small but with an upper bound just over the 10% relative scale; unresolved/deferred. Overall, the accepted dependency-specific effects are one to two orders of magnitude larger than these control estimates, so the controls make pure global technical confounding less likely, but two controls remain too imprecise to claim exact nulls.\n\nMultiplicity matters. The new wave contains many related checks, but the accepted large effects have intervals so far from zero that family-wise or Bonferroni-style caution would not overturn them. Borderline control/interaction claims are not upgraded to accept because their intervals remain compatible with null or small effects. record.narrative: The accepted associations are large and internally robust, but they remain observational and potentially context-dependent. This wave first tests the dominant Avana-adenocarcinoma context jointly, which combines technical homogeneity and biological homogeneity. I then probe biologically motivated pathway hypotheses: p53 pathway dependence on MDM2; MAPK-pathway interplay among BRAF and KRAS; receptor-tyrosine-kinase dependencies involving EGFR, ERBB2, and PTEN; and co-mutation interaction between KEAP1 and TP53 on NFE2L2. I also test receptor and oncogenic-pathway mean differences within the dominant adenocarcinoma subtype for KRAS mutation, EGFR amplification, and ERBB2 amplification to see whether global null or borderline effects hide subtype-specific effects. Direction convention remains that more negative raw dependency scores mean stronger dependency; I set direction accordingly. Practical importance will be judged by whether intervals exclude near-zero and contain at least about a 10% relative difference on the outcome scale, while accepting that the four already accepted large effects clear this threshold comfortably. All new claims are unresolved because no direct evidence yet exists for these specific comparisons.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All new estimates were interpreted on the signed scale supplied by the controller, with direction-1 positive values indicating a raw more-negative outcome and therefore stronger CRISPR dependency, and direction-1 negative values indicating weaker dependency; direction-1 positive values indicate weaker dependency where the outcome scale is interpreted through the hypothesized direction, as in the TP53-USP7 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 analyses. H24 is the key new positive robustness result: non-Avana SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA4-wild-type cells have signed effect 0.801 with 95% Welch interval 0.748 to 0.853, well beyond zero and practical significance on the SMARCA2 scale, so I accept it, though I keep it active because I request independent validation for this library-restricted result. H36 and H37 also strongly support the TP53-USP7 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 associations in non-Avana cells, so they are accepted and closed as consistency checks. H41 shows that MSI-high cells in the mutation-burden 10 or greater subgroup retain a very large WRN dependency effect, signed 0.768 with interval 0.721 to 0.815, so this refinement is accepted and closed. H17 does not support ARID1A loss as a meaningful predictor of stronger SMARCA2 dependency; the signed upper bound is only 0.023, below the approximate 10% absolute mean scale of dependency_SMARCA2, so I reject that hypothesis. H20 similarly rejects the pre-specified adenocarcinoma-specific enhancement interaction because the signed upper bound is 0.020, below the practical threshold for SMARCA2, while the main SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association remains large in both subgroups. The remaining new interaction or borderline controls are not decisive: USP7-by-subtype interaction, KRAS-by-STK11 interaction, NFE2L2-by-subtype interaction, and NFE2L2-by-TP53-loss interaction are inconclusive and not prioritized; direct TP53-loss MDM2 dependency in Avana and EGFR-amplification EGFR dependency within adenocarcinoma remain unresolved and deferred because their intervals cross zero and include practical effect sizes. I request validation for H24 because non-Avana SMARCA4-SMARCA2 robustness is important but rests on a smaller library subset; independent evidence would materially strengthen the conclusion that the association is not an Avana-library artifact. These remain dataset associations only, not causal or externally generalizable claims.
